- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >80), model often fails to correct downward quickly; apply a lagged mean reversion bias to dampen overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model underreacts; increase forecast downward by 1–2% to align with sentiment shift.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period drops (last 5–7 days of forecast) — apply a downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model exhibits erratic behavior — use a smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce noise.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overfits recent trends; apply a 10–15% downward adjustment if recent 5-day average is rising sharply.
